1	"""Durable JSON-file persistence for the device store.
2	
3	The whole server state is kept in one versioned JSON document. A missing file
4	is created on first use; a corrupted file or a document whose version is not
5	understood makes the server refuse to start (state is never silently
6	discarded). Every change is written atomically: serialize to a temporary file
7	in the same directory, ``fsync`` it, take a hard-link backup of the current
8	target, ``os.replace`` it over the target, then ``fsync`` the parent
9	directory, so a crash never leaves a half-written or un-renamed state file.
10	
11	Persistence is transactional with respect to the in-memory store: the change
12	hook fires while the store lock is held (the mutation is visible but not yet
13	committed to callers). When the durable write succeeds it becomes the new
14	last-known-good state. When writing the temporary file, ``fsync`` or the
15	atomic replace fails (an :class:`OSError`), the previous last-known-good state
16	is restored into memory under the same lock and
17	:class:`PersistenceUnavailable` is raised so the HTTP layer answers
18	503/field=data_file; the failed mutation therefore never advances either
19	memory or the file.
20	
21	After the replace has landed, a failed directory fsync first rolls the rename
22	back: the pinned old inode is renamed over the target and a second directory
23	fsync flushes the rollback. When that rollback itself cannot be completed
24	durably — the rollback rename fails, or the second fsync fails — the failure
25	stays *decidable*: the old inode is kept under a ``.state-*.bak`` backup and
26	the new snapshot is taken off the formal path (parked under a
27	``.state-*.quarantine`` name the recovery scan never promotes, or deleted), so
28	the formal path is missing. The store is then marked degraded and reports 503
29	for the failed request.
30	
31	The degraded store also heals itself *within the same process*: the next
32	persist-able write runs, inside the storage lock, :meth:`JsonStateStore.heal`
33	before saving — the unique pinned ``.bak`` is fully verified (version=1,
34	commit generation, the complete-transaction sections, every cross-entity /
35	cursor / nonce / audit-chain semantic check, and exact equality with the
36	last committed in-memory state) and atomically promoted back onto the formal
37	path, same-transaction leftovers (``.quarantine``/``.tmp``) are removed, and
38	only then is that one triggering request committed (a single consecutive
39	``commit_seq`` advance). The request that originally got 503 is never
40	replayed; the healed commit carries only the later, current request. A
41	corrupt, dangling or ambiguous backup is refused promotion: the request gets
42	503/field=data_file, memory is rolled back, the formal path stays missing,
43	no leftover or generation moves, and the next write retries the heal. A
44	valid formal file always takes precedence over every backup. Restart
45	recovery remains the fallback that promotes the pinned backup.
46	
47	When even the decidable fallback cannot be achieved — the un-committed new
48	snapshot can be neither renamed aside nor deleted, so the formal path cannot be
49	proven missing — the store enters the *blocking state* (a sibling
50	``.state-*.block`` marker persists it across restarts). It never serves
51	that residual formal file as authoritative: every subsequent write is
52	503/field=data_file, in this process and after a restart, until the path is
53	vacated with exactly one verifiable backup (heal/restart then promote it and
54	clear the marker), or a file provably equal to the committed state is restored
55	onto the formal path (a valid formal always wins). Two or more
56	verifiable backups make promotion ambiguous and are likewise refused rather than picked by
57	name or mtime.
58	
59	A crash between steps can leave ``.state-*.tmp`` (staged document) or
60	``.state-*.bak`` (pinned previous inode) files beside the target. At the next
61	:func:`attach_persistence` these are resolved by
62	:func:`recover_crash_leftovers`: a valid formal file stays authoritative and
63	the leftovers are removed; with the formal file missing the highest
64	``commit_seq`` leftover that parses as version=1, carries the cursor and
65	``key_events`` sections (the footprint of one complete durable transaction),
66	and passes every semantic restore check is atomically recovered into place
67	(modification time newest-first breaks equal generations, and files without
68	the field keep the legacy newest-mtime rule); with none valid the leftovers
69	are removed and an empty state is created. An existing-but-corrupt formal
70	file still makes startup refuse rather than being silently overwritten.
71	
72	Every document carries a strictly-consecutive top-level ``commit_seq``: the
73	first empty state is written at 0 and each successful durable transaction
74	advances it exactly once (a failed write consumes no generation). A legacy
75	version=1 file without the field loads as generation 0; a present field must
76	be a non-negative integer or startup refuses (bool, negative, float and
77	string values are rejected) with the file untouched.
78	
79	Beside the state file every normal commit maintains an append-only integrity
80	sidecar at ``<state>.integrity`` (a compact version=1 JSON document with one
81	``commit_seq``/``state_hash``/``prev_hash``/``hash`` entry per committed
82	generation), written in the same locked two-file transaction. The state
83	document records the format with ``integrity_log_version=1``; a legacy file
84	without that marker and without a sidecar still starts and anchors the chain
85	on its first commit, while any marker/sidecar disagreement or a broken /
86	tail-mismatched chain makes startup refuse with both files untouched. The
87	sidecar backs ``GET /v1/persistence/integrity/history`` and its ascending,
88	cursor-paged variant ``GET /v1/persistence/integrity/history/page``
89	(``commit_seq > after``, at most ``limit``).
90	"""
91	from __future__ import annotations
92	
93	import copy
94	import errno
95	import hashlib
96	import json
97	import os
98	import sys
99	import tempfile
100	from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
101	
102	from .storage import (
103	    DeviceStore,
104	    canonical_integrity_snapshot,
105	    integrity_state_hash,
106	)
107	
108	if TYPE_CHECKING:  # pragma: no cover - typing only
109	    from .service import DeviceService
110	
111	#: Persistence format version understood by this build.
112	STATE_VERSION = 1
113	
114	#: Integrity sidecar log format version.
115	INTEGRITY_LOG_VERSION = 1
116	#: State-document field recording which integrity-sidecar format this file's
117	#: store maintains (absent on legacy documents that predate the sidecar).
118	INTEGRITY_LOG_VERSION_KEY = "integrity_log_version"
119	#: Suffix appended to the state-file path for its integrity-history sidecar.
120	_INTEGRITY_LOG_SUFFIX = ".integrity"
121	
122	#: Temporary-snapshot name parts, mirrored when scanning crash leftovers
123	#: (see :meth:`JsonStateStore.save`).
124	_TMP_PREFIX = ".state-"
125	_TMP_SUFFIX = ".tmp"
126	#: Suffix of the pre-replace hard-link backup pinning the previous inode.
127	_BAK_SUFFIX = ".bak"
128	#: Suffix of a new snapshot taken off the formal path when the rollback
129	#: itself cannot be completed durably. Such a file is deliberately *not* a
130	#: crash-recovery candidate (the scan only promotes ``.tmp``/``.bak``): the
131	#: transaction it staged was already reported failed and rolled back in
132	#: memory, so it must never be resurrected at the next startup.
133	_QUARANTINE_SUFFIX = ".quarantine"
134	#: Suffix of the durable marker left when a failed transaction could not be made
135	#: decidable: the formal path could not be vacated, so a possibly-un-committed
136	#: residual formal file sits beside a ``.bak`` of the last committed
137	#: inode. While such a marker exists the store is in the *blocking state*:
138	#: writes are refused (503/field=data_file) and the residual formal file is
139	#: never treated as authoritative, until an operator removes the marker (after resolving
140	#: the on-disk state) — or until heal finds the formal path missing with
141	#: exactly one verifiable backup, at which point it clears the marker itself.
142	_BLOCK_SUFFIX = ".block"
143	
144	#: Top-level commit-generation field. Every successful durable transaction
145	#: writes a document whose ``commit_seq`` is exactly one higher than the
146	#: previous one; the first (empty) state is created at 0. A legacy version-1
147	#: file written before this field loads as if it carried 0.
148	COMMIT_SEQ_KEY = "commit_seq"
149	
150	
151	def _valid_commit_seq(value: Any) -> bool:
152	    """A commit generation is a non-negative JSON integer (never a bool)."""
153	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) and value >= 0
154	
155	
156	def _commit_seq_of(document: Dict[str, Any]) -> int:
157	    """Rank a candidate by its commit generation; a missing/malformed one is 0.
158	
159	    Leftover snapshots are ranked leniently here (a leftover without the field
160	    predates commit generations and sorts at generation 0); the *formal*
161	    file's field is validated strictly by :meth:`JsonStateStore.load`.
162	    """
163	    value = document.get(COMMIT_SEQ_KEY, 0)
164	    return value if _valid_commit_seq(value) else 0
165	
166	
167	class StateFileError(Exception):
168	    """The state file is missing fields, corrupt, or has an unknown version."""
169	
170	
171	class PersistenceUnavailable(Exception):
172	    """A durable write failed; the transaction was rolled back in memory.
173	
174	    The in-memory store was restored to the last successfully persisted state
175	    under the store lock, the previous state file is intact, and the temporary
176	    file was removed. The HTTP layer reports this as 503/field=data_file.
177	    """
178	
179	
180	class IntegrityCheckError(Exception):
181	    """A read-only integrity probe could not verify the state file.
182	
183	    The file is missing/unreadable, cannot be parsed as a version-1 JSON
184	    object, carries an invalid ``commit_seq``, fails the full semantic
185	    restore, or its canonical snapshot differs from the in-memory state.
186	    Nothing is read into the live store and no file, inode, cursor or
187	    generation is touched; the HTTP layer reports this as
188	    503/field=data_file.
189	    """
190	
191	
192	class IntegrityLogError(Exception):
193	    """The integrity-history sidecar is missing or fails every check.
194	
195	    Raised at startup when the ``integrity_log_version`` marker and the
196	    sibling ``<state>.integrity`` log disagree (one present without the
197	    other, or an unknown marker value), or when the log document is
198	    structurally invalid, its hash chain is broken, an entry hash does not
199	    verify, or its last entry does not match the state file's generation.
200	    The store refuses to start and leaves both files untouched.
201	    """
202	
203	
204	def _integrity_entry_hash(commit_seq: int, state_hash: str,
205	                          prev_hash: str) -> str:
206	    """Hash one integrity-log entry: the entry without ``hash``.
207	
208	    Keys are sorted, separators compact and Unicode written literally; the
209	    UTF-8 bytes are SHA-256 digested to lowercase hex, exactly like the
210	    key-audit event chain.
211	    """
212	    document = {"commit_seq": commit_seq, "state_hash": state_hash,
213	                "prev_hash": prev_hash}
214	    canonical = json.dumps(document, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"),
215	                           ensure_ascii=False)
216	    return hashlib.sha256(canonical.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
217	
218	
219	def _is_hex64(value: Any) -> bool:
220	    return isinstance(value, str) and len(value) == 64 \
221	        and all(ch in "0123456789abcdef" for ch in value)
222	
223	
224	def _read_integrity_log(path: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
225	    """Parse the integrity sidecar, or ``None`` when it does not exist.
226	
227	    Returns the raw parsed document (validation happens in
228	    :func:`_verify_integrity_log`). Unreadable/undecodable files raise
229	    :class:`IntegrityLogError` rather than returning ``None``: only a
230	    genuinely absent file means "no sidecar".
231	    """
232	    try:
233	        with open(path, "rb") as handle:
234	            raw = handle.read()
235	    except FileNotFoundError:
236	        return None
237	    except OSError as error:
238	        raise IntegrityLogError(
239	            f"cannot read integrity log {path}: {error}") from None
240	    try:
241	        document = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
242	    except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error:
243	        raise IntegrityLogError(
244	            f"integrity log is not valid JSON: {path} ({error})") from None
245	    if not isinstance(document, dict):
246	        raise IntegrityLogError("integrity log must be a JSON object")
247	    return document
248	
249	
250	def _verify_integrity_log(document: Dict[str, Any]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
251	    """Fully validate a parsed integrity sidecar; return its entries.
252	
253	    Enforces top-level shape (``version == 1``, an ``entries`` list, no
254	    extra keys), each entry's shape and key order, strictly-consecutive
255	    ``commit_seq`` values in ascending order, lowercase-hex hashes, an empty
256	    ``prev_hash`` on the first entry chained to the previous ``hash`` on
257	    every later one, and that each entry's ``hash`` is the SHA-256 of its
258	    ``commit_seq``/``state_hash``/``prev_hash`` (sorted-key compact JSON).
259	
260	    The first entry may carry any non-negative generation: a legacy file
261	    loaded without a sidecar anchors the chain at the generation of the
262	    first write that enables it; every later entry is exactly one
263	    generation higher. Binding of the chain *tail* to the state file's
264	    current generation and hash is the caller's last-entry check.
265	    Raises :class:`IntegrityLogError` on the first violation.
266	    """
267	    if list(document) != ["version", "entries"]:
268	        raise IntegrityLogError(
269	            "integrity log must have exactly the keys 'version' and "
270	            "'entries' in order")
271	    version = document.get("version")
272	    if not isinstance(version, int) or isinstance(version, bool):
273	        raise IntegrityLogError("integrity log is missing a numeric version")
274	    if version != INTEGRITY_LOG_VERSION:
275	        raise IntegrityLogError(
276	            f"unsupported integrity log version: {version} "
277	            f"(this server supports {INTEGRITY_LOG_VERSION})")
278	    entries = document.get("entries")
279	    if not isinstance(entries, list):
280	        raise IntegrityLogError("integrity log 'entries' must be a list")
281	    verified: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
282	    prev_hash = ""
283	    anchor_seq: Optional[int] = None
284	    for index, entry in enumerate(entries):
285	        where = f"integrity log entries[{index}]"
286	        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
287	            raise IntegrityLogError(f"{where} must be an object")
288	        if list(entry) != ["commit_seq", "state_hash", "prev_hash", "hash"]:
289	            raise IntegrityLogError(
290	                f"{where} must have exactly the keys 'commit_seq', "
291	                f"'state_hash', 'prev_hash', 'hash' in order")
292	        commit_seq = entry["commit_seq"]
293	        state_hash = entry["state_hash"]
294	        entry_prev = entry["prev_hash"]
295	        entry_hash = entry["hash"]
296	        if not isinstance(commit_seq, int) or isinstance(commit_seq, bool) \
297	                or commit_seq < 0:
298	            raise IntegrityLogError(
299	                f"{where}.commit_seq must be a non-negative integer")
300	        if not _is_hex64(state_hash):
301	            raise IntegrityLogError(
302	                f"{where}.state_hash must be a 64-character lowercase hex "
303	                f"string")
304	        if not isinstance(entry_prev, str):
305	            raise IntegrityLogError(f"{where}.prev_hash must be a string")
306	        if not _is_hex64(entry_hash):

372	def _gate_integrity_sidecar(
373	        state_store: "JsonStateStore",
374	        document: Dict[str, Any]) -> Tuple[bool, List[Dict[str, Any]]]:
375	    """Validate the marker/sidecar pairing of a loaded state document.
376	
377	    Returns ``(enabled, entries)``. A legacy document without the
378	    ``integrity_log_version`` marker and without a sidecar starts with
379	    ``(False, [])`` — the first write migrates it. Every other arrangement
380	    refuses startup with :class:`IntegrityLogError` and leaves both files
381	    untouched:
382	
383	    * marker present but sidecar missing, or vice versa;
384	    * a marker whose value is not the integer ``1``;
385	    * a sidecar that fails the structure/chain/hash validation, is empty, or
386	      whose last entry does not carry the document's generation and the
387	      document payload's canonical state hash.
388	    """
389	    marker_present = INTEGRITY_LOG_VERSION_KEY in document
390	    try:
391	        log_document = _read_integrity_log(state_store.integrity_log_path)
392	    except IntegrityLogError:
393	        raise
394	    sidecar_present = log_document is not None
395	    if not marker_present and not sidecar_present:
396	        return False, []
397	    if marker_present and not sidecar_present:
398	        raise IntegrityLogError(
399	            "state document carries 'integrity_log_version' but the "
400	            f"integrity sidecar {state_store.integrity_log_path} is missing")
401	    if sidecar_present and not marker_present:
402	        raise IntegrityLogError(
403	            "an integrity sidecar exists beside a state document without "
404	            "'integrity_log_version'")
405	    marker = document[INTEGRITY_LOG_VERSION_KEY]
406	    if not isinstance(marker, int) or isinstance(marker, bool) \
407	            or marker != INTEGRITY_LOG_VERSION:
408	        raise IntegrityLogError(
409	            f"unsupported integrity_log_version marker: {marker!r}")
410	    entries = _verify_integrity_log(log_document)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
411	    if not entries:
412	        raise IntegrityLogError("integrity sidecar carries no entries")
413	    payload = {key: value for key, value in document.items()
414	               if key not in ("version", COMMIT_SEQ_KEY,
415	                              INTEGRITY_LOG_VERSION_KEY)}
416	    try:
417	        fresh = DeviceStore()
418	        fresh.restore_state(copy.deepcopy(payload))
419	        canonical = canonical_integrity_snapshot(fresh.snapshot_state())
420	    except (ValueError, TypeError) as error:
421	        raise IntegrityLogError(
422	            f"integrity sidecar state cannot be restored: {error}") from None
423	    expected_hash = integrity_state_hash(canonical)
424	    generation = _commit_seq_of(document)
425	    last = entries[-1]
426	    if last["commit_seq"] != generation:
427	        raise IntegrityLogError(
428	            "integrity sidecar last entry commit_seq "
429	            f"{last['commit_seq']} does not match the state document "
430	            f"generation {generation}")
431	    if last["state_hash"] != expected_hash:
432	        raise IntegrityLogError(
433	            "integrity sidecar last entry state_hash does not match the "
434	            "state document")
435	    return True, entries

771	    def heal(self, baseline: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:

773	
774	        Called under the store lock by the persistence hook at the start of
775	        the next persist-able write after an undecidable write failure. The

777	        generation exactly one below the next save's generation, the whole
778	        cross-entity/cursor/nonce/audit-chain semantic restore, and exact
779	        equality with the process's last committed in-memory state — before
780	        it is promoted. Promotion is a same-directory *hard link*: the backup
781	        name keeps pinning the inode until the formal directory entry is
782	        fsync-durable, so a crash at this instant leaves either a valid
783	        formal file or the still-present backup, never neither. Only then are
784	        the same-transaction leftovers (redundant backups, staged ``.tmp``
785	        snapshots and the un-committed ``.quarantine``) removed.
786	
787	        A later write commit still goes through the normal atomic
788	        :meth:`save`, so healing consumes no generation: the healed commit
789	        advances ``commit_seq`` exactly once and carries only that triggering
790	        request — the earlier request that got 503 is never replayed.
791	
792	        Raises :class:`OSError` (mapped to 503/field=data_file by the caller)
793	        when no verifiable backup exists, two or more verifiable candidates
794	        exist (promotion is refused outright — choosing by name or mtime is
795	        forbidden), or the promotion cannot be made durable; in every such
796	        case the formal path stays missing, no leftover and no generation
797	        moves, :attr:`degraded` (or :attr:`blocked`) stays set, and the next
798	        write retries this heal. A formal file that reappeared valid and matching
799	        always takes precedence over every backup — but only in the *degraded*
800	        state. In the *blocking* state a residual formal file is never served as
801	        authoritative: heal refuses while it occupies the path, and only leaves the

808	        leftovers = _leftover_tmp_paths(directory, self.path)

939	        document must parse as JSON, be an object stamped ``version=1``, and
940	        carry either no ``commit_seq`` (a legacy file, generation 0) or a

959	            try:
960	                with open(self.path, "rb") as handle:
961	                    raw = handle.read()
962	            except OSError as error:
963	                raise IntegrityCheckError(
964	                    f"cannot read state file {self.path}: {error}") from None
965	            try:
966	                document = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
967	            except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error:
968	                raise IntegrityCheckError(
969	                    f"state file is not valid JSON: {self.path} ({error})") \
970	                    from None

972	                raise IntegrityCheckError(
973	                    "state document must be a JSON object")
974	            version = document.get("version")
975	            if not isinstance(version, int) or isinstance(version, bool):
976	                raise IntegrityCheckError(
977	                    "state document is missing a numeric 'version'")

981	                    f"(this server supports {STATE_VERSION})")

986	                    f"non-negative integer")

988	                       if key not in ("version", COMMIT_SEQ_KEY,
989	                                      INTEGRITY_LOG_VERSION_KEY)}

992	        def expected_generation() -> int:

996	            # can never be sampled from different linearization points.
997	            return self.commit_seq - 1

1173	def _directory_fsync_unsupported(error: OSError) -> bool:
1174	    """Classify *error* as "this platform/filesystem cannot fsync a directory".
1175	
1176	    Some POSIX network or special filesystems reject ``fsync`` on a
1177	    directory fd with ``EINVAL`` (others use ``ENOTSUP``/``EOPNOTSUPP``);
1178	    on Windows a directory cannot be opened for this at all and the CRT
1179	    fails with ``EACCES`` (older runtimes raise ``EISDIR``). None of these
1180	    means the data write itself failed — the file fsync and the atomic
1181	    rename already landed — so the directory flush is safely skipped
1182	    instead of failing (and rolling back) the whole transaction. Genuine
1183	    I/O errors (``EIO``, ``EBADF``, permission problems elsewhere, ...)
1184	    still propagate.
1185	    """
1186	    unsupported = {errno.EINVAL, errno.ENOTSUP,
1187	                   getattr(errno, "EOPNOTSUPP", None)}
1188	    if error.errno in unsupported:
1189	        return True
1190	    if sys.platform == "win32" and error.errno in (errno.EACCES, errno.EISDIR):
1191	        return True
1192	    return False

1195	def _fsync_directory(directory: str) -> bool:
1196	    """Flush *directory*'s metadata so a recent rename survives a crash.
1197	
1198	    Returns ``True`` when the flush ran. When the platform or underlying
1199	    filesystem cannot fsync directories, the capability is safely skipped
1200	    (returns ``False``) without reporting a failure; every other
1201	    :class:`OSError` propagates to the caller. On platforms without
1202	    ``O_DIRECTORY`` the plain read-only open still works.
1203	    """
1204	    flags = os.O_RDONLY
1205	    try:
1206	        dir_fd = os.open(directory, flags)
1207	    except OSError as error:
1208	        if _directory_fsync_unsupported(error):
1209	            return False
1210	        raise
1211	    try:
1212	        os.fsync(dir_fd)
1213	    except OSError as error:
1214	        if _directory_fsync_unsupported(error):
1215	            return False
1216	        raise
1217	    finally:
1218	        os.close(dir_fd)
1219	    return True

1287	    the inode under a fresh backup name, then drop *target* (a second hard
1288	    link to the same inode, so the unlink loses nothing), recreating the
1289	    same "formal missing + old-inode .bak" triage a plain rollback failure
1290	    leaves. Returns ``True`` when the formal path was vacated. If the inode

1293	    not mark the store degraded while a good file is authoritative.
1294	    """

1297	                                      suffix=_BAK_SUFFIX)
1298	        os.close(fd)
1299	        os.unlink(backup)
1300	        os.link(target, backup)
1301	    except OSError:
